extra.message: The 'username' query parameter from the GET /select endpoint is interpolated directly into a SQL string via an f-string and passed to db.execute() (run_sql_query). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL, e.g. username=\" OR \"1\"=\"1, to dump all rows or perform other SQL injection attacks.

In PUT /user, all user-supplied fields (name, username, password, address, email, contact) are interpolated directly into an INSERT SQL string via an f-string and executed with run_sql_query(commit=True). Any of these fields can break out of the quoted string context and inject arbitrary SQL.

In DELETE /user, the 'username' query parameter is interpolated directly into a DELETE SQL statement via an f-string and executed. An attacker can inject SQL to delete arbitrary rows or alter the query (e.g. username=\" OR \"1\"=\"1 deletes all users).

In DELETE /user (user body branch), user.address is interpolated directly (and unquoted) into a DELETE SQL statement via an f-string and executed. This allows trivial SQL injection through the address field of the request body.

POST /find reads the raw JSON request body and passes it unmodified as the query object to MontyDB users.find() in get_nosql_users(). An attacker can supply MongoDB query operators (e.g. {\"username\": {\"$ne\": null}} or {\"$where\": ...}) to bypass intended filtering and exfiltrate arbitrary user records (NoSQL injection).

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic (NoSQL Injection)

extra.message: POST /reset deletes the entire SQL database file and removes the NoSQL database directory, then re-initializes them, with no authentication or authorization. Any unauthenticated remote user can destroy all stored data, causing data loss / denial of service.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: State-changing and data-reading endpoints (PUT /user, DELETE /user, GET /select, GET/POST /find) have no authentication or authorization controls. Any anonymous user can create, delete, and read arbitrary user records including PII (name, address, email, contact).

User passwords are hashed with unsalted MD5 (md5(user.password.encode()).hexdigest()) before storage. MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsalted, making the stored password hashes vulnerable to brute-force and rainbow-table attacks. A password-specific KDF (bcrypt/scrypt/argon2) should be used instead.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: Seed/demo user passwords are hashed with unsalted MD5 (md5(fake.password().encode()).hexdigest()). MD5 is a broken, fast hash unsuitable for password storage.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: remove() and rmtree() are invoked on fixed database paths without verifying their existence after potential prior deletion, and with no authorization; combined with the unauthenticated /reset endpoint this enables denial of service through repeated destruction of application state.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
